analysis.title: What's Next For Data Centers After The Blue Tsunami: Goldman Sees Moratoria Freezing 45% Of Capacity As Texas Pulls The Plug
key_insights: Goldman (Hatzius) expects Democratic wins at state and local level to lead to short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion. Federal outlook is less likely to change because AI regulation would still need bipartisan Senate support and a veto override.

Goldman says the states where Democrats are likely to further restrict data centers hold roughly 45% of planned US data center capacity, with Texas alone about 25%. Goldman expects new governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan to impose conditional moratoria pending new legislation.

Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott about 52.8% to 45.7% in the Texas governor race on a platform centered on an immediate moratorium on new data centers. Polymarket gave her a 24.5% chance in mid-October, and BofA saw little evidence equities priced a change.

Texas approvals have been frozen by executive directive since August. Wells Fargo (Revich) says the election converts the pause from one tied to an audit into one tied to legislation. ERCOT targets a December 10 audit filing, the Legislature convenes January 12 and its regular session ends May 31, 2027. SemiAnalysis estimates a freeze through the session would run about eight months from September and could approach a year.

Lt. Governor-elect Vikki Goodwin (D) also supports pausing new data centers and the Lt. Governor controls the Texas Senate's legislative agenda. Jefferies had called her race a potentially bigger under-appreciated risk than the governor's, and says Texas is 'Not business as usual.'

Jefferies calls data centers a bipartisan affordability issue, with cost-causer-pays platforms in OH, GA, MI, WI, IA and TX. It expects anti-data center efforts in many state legislatures in 2027, and Virginia moratorium bills are advancing ahead of the January 13 session.

Texas share of US data center pipeline varies by source: Wells Fargo (Tusa) about 81 GW or about 20% of cumulative adjusted pipeline, Goldman via Cleanview 26.7%, Jefferies citing Wells Fargo about 27%. SemiAnalysis has Texas adding close to 30% of all US gigawatts in 2028.

GLJ Research (Johnson) estimates about 13 GW of Texas capacity is immediately exposed (Jefferies via Bear Traps: 13.3 GW). Projects with power, permits and steel continue, those with power but no state environmental permits slip 12 to 18 months, and those with neither may go to Louisiana, Oklahoma or nowhere.
ERCOT's large-load queue hit about 474 GW in August, roughly 90% data centers and more than five times the grid's all-time peak, so a large share of the pipeline is speculative.

Wells Fargo tracks about 3 GW of Caterpillar and Cummins capacity on Texas projects seemingly on hold. Cummins' entire 2.0 GW tracked prime position is the Circe Energy behind-the-meter West Texas campus. At least about 1.1 GW and $1.2B of CAT turbine content sits on Texas projects awaiting state action, led by Microsoft/Chevron's Project Kilby and Stargate's Abilene.

The September TCEQ directive reaches air permits, so on-site behind-the-meter generation is also caught. Power generation lead times extend into 2030, beyond the roughly 18 months of visibility an air permit provides, so OEM delivery slots may be deferred or resequenced to other customers.

Wells Fargo (Revich) admits its work treated financing as available and says CDS tracked since September suggest rising risk. The article says delays leave bridge loans that cannot be termed out, citing a $15B bridge loan on Anthropic's Nexus Hubbard campus that banks were stuck holding.

Bear Traps (McDonald) cites Wells Fargo math that every 10% haircut to Texas data centers is a 1.6% hit to total AI capex. The article extends this to about 4% for a 25% haircut and about 8% if 50%+ of Texas projects are cancelled, all else equal.

Hyperscaler capex: the five biggest spent $237B in a single quarter, up 99% y/y, with 2027 guided higher. AI investment added 1.2% to recent US GDP growth, and debt funds about a third of the build per the quoted commentary.

Goldman (Hatzius) expects the issue to fade in importance and moratoria not to be long-lived. Goldman's Davenport sees Texas as a timing risk rather than a longer-term opportunity risk, and Jefferies' headline is 'Demand moves right, not away.' The author disagrees and leans toward a freeze lasting at least through May 31, 2027.

Wolfe (Senyek) says the Texas result and Democratic wins spell trouble for the AI trade in the very short term and that Texas could be a model for opposition elsewhere. Data center construction spending is at record highs and year-to-date exceeds 2025's full-year total.

Goldman now sees behind-the-meter power supplying 25% of all data centers by 2030. Wells Fargo cites Louisiana's newly elected 4-1 Republican PSC as the most constructive setup for Entergy's buildout.

market_movers.rationale: Wells Fargo tracks at least about 1.1 GW and $1.2B of CAT turbine content on Texas projects awaiting state action. Delivery slots could be deferred or resequenced.
Cummins' entire 2.0 GW tracked prime position is the Circe Energy behind-the-meter West Texas campus, with deliveries through 2030, and is now exposed to the Texas permit freeze.
Wells Fargo calls Louisiana's newly elected 4-1 Republican PSC the most constructive setup for Entergy's buildout, as projects without Texas permits may relocate to Louisiana.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman and Jefferies see a timing delay, not lost demand. Wells Fargo, Wolfe and the article see near-term risk to permits, power equipment orders and financing.
Goldman's Davenport sees Texas as primarily a risk to timing of development rather than the longer-term opportunity.

earnings_insights: Wolfe's Senyek liked the AMD and SMCI prints reported the night before (Nov 4), but gives no figures in this article.
Five biggest hyperscalers reported combined quarterly capex of $237B, up 99% y/y, with 2027 guided higher across all of them (as cited by Bear Traps, reported).

macro_indicators.indicator: AI-related investment contribution to US GDP growth
macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited by Bear Traps as the direct GDP input at risk if the capex curve flattens because of Texas permitting.
Capex is rising, so a Texas freeze would hit a still-growing GDP input.

macro_indicators.indicator: Wells Fargo sensitivity: AI capex hit per 10% Texas haircut
macro_indicators.interpretation: A 25% Texas haircut implies about a 4% hit to AI capex and 50% implies about 8% (article extension).
Converts the Texas data center pause from an audit-linked one to a legislation-linked one.

risk_factors: Texas freeze lasting through the legislative session ending May 31, 2027, possibly close to a year per SemiAnalysis.
Copycat moratoria in Georgia, Ohio, Michigan and other states, with Virginia bills advancing.
OEM turbine and engine delivery slots deferred or resequenced because permits lag 2029-30 delivery dates.
Financing stress: debt funds about a third of the build, bridge loans cannot be termed out, and CDS are rising.
Revenue deferral: BNEF's roughly $1.76B per GW per month on about 13 GW slipping 12-18 months, with the article estimating a range of roughly $275B-$410B pushed out (assuming all capacity is real).
Implementation detail on Hinojosa's rate freeze is thin, per Jefferies.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures sold off on the Texas result, then NQ rallied 929 points off the overnight lows. The author expects the rally not to last.
Pre-election markets gave the stricter-regulation side a 35% chance in Texas (26.7% of planned capacity) and 92% in Michigan, per Goldman's exhibit.
Wells Fargo has tracked CDS since September that suggest rising financing risk in the AI buildout.
geopolitical: Democratic wins in the US midterms: governorships in Texas, Georgia, Michigan, Nevada, Ohio, plus trifectas in Pennsylvania and likely Arizona, with House and Senate majorities per Goldman.
Federal data center and AI regulation unlikely to change because it needs bipartisan Senate support and must overcome a veto, so action shifts to state capitols.
Texas Lt. Governor Goodwin (D, first in 27 years), Senator-elect Talarico and Railroad Commissioner Rosenthal (first Democrat in 32 years) add to the Texas policy shift.
Virginia moratorium bills advancing ahead of the January 13 session.
cross_bank_references: Goldman Hatzius: moratoria 'will not be long-lived'; the article disputes this.
Goldman Lightowler: Hinojosa 'will not lift the freeze until more comprehensive regulation is passed.'
BofA: 'little evidence that equities reflect any probability of a change in the governor's mansion.'
Wells Fargo cites SemiAnalysis on freeze duration; Jefferies cites the Wells Fargo ~27% Texas figure.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Hatzius expects moratoria to not be long-lived because data centers are low on voters' priority list. Jefferies says 'Demand moves right, not away' with pragmatic new governors, and announcements are possible as soon as 1Q27 in select states.
tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa says the freeze stays until new laws pass, the Democratic Lt. Governor who controls the Senate agenda also wants a pause, the Legislature meets on a biennial calendar, and financing is already strained. The article leans toward a freeze through at least May 31, 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deal or special session before the Legislature's regular session ends May 31, 2027, or a reopening of permitting after ERCOT's December 10 audit filing.

tension_points.bull_case: Construction put in place for data centers hit new highs and year-to-date exceeds 2025's total dollar amount despite moratoria. Projects with power, permits and steel keep going.
tension_points.bear_case: Every 10% Texas haircut is a 1.6% hit to total AI capex, and 50%+ cancellations would be about 8%. Hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative and debt funds about a third of the build.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Texas permitting reopening after the Legislature acts, or a capex curve that keeps rising through the session.
